name: UACE-4: Unexpected Legitimate Command Sent
description: A machine-learning rule over the command feed: the job learns the normal command vocabulary system-wide and scores any command that is rare — a memory poke, EEPROM enable, or clock jam stands out against the routine housekeeping. Catches a dangerous command even when it is not in the hazardous catalog; source.ip/target_name are the influencers and operator attribution is done by the AI agent from the portal log. Bound to the defcon-insider-rare-command job.
author: Elastic
false_positives: A new but authorized account, a first-of-campaign maintenance command, or an infrequent scheduled command can score as rare. Tune per mission via detection exceptions at deployment.
note:
## SPARTA Investigation Guide

### Detection logic
A machine-learning anomaly job (`rare` command.name, population-level) over the command feed. It learns the system-wide command vocabulary and flags a command that is rare — a dangerous command not in the hazardous catalog still stands out. Influenced by source.ip/target_name; the command feed carries no operator identity, so attribution is done at query time by the AI agent from the portal registration log. This surfaces UACE-4: an unexpected but legitimate command sent.

### Framework reference
- **Tactic:** Initial Access
- **Technique IA-0007:** [Compromise Ground System](https://sparta.aerospace.org/technique/IA-0007/)
- **Indicator of Behavior UACE-4:** Unexpected legitimate command sent.

### How to validate this alert
Review the anomaly's influencers (command.name, source.ip, target_name). Correlate with the hazardous-command and flooding rules and the SPACECOP IDS alert, and ask the AI agent to attribute the command to a registered operator. See spartastixkb for countermeasures.
